_meta.note: Captured off the wire: `codex-acp` 1.11.0 driven over stdio, agent-to-client lines verbatim and in order. A slice of one turn reaching four of the seven required classes -- the initialize response with agentInfo.version, the _auth/status_update the adapter sends before session/new, the session/new response with a sessionId and its configOptions, agent_message_chunk frames, a usage_update, the session_info_update frames carrying _meta.codex, and the stopReason response with a usage block. The recording home directory reads as ~; nothing was removed. The three tool classes are absent because no tool call happened: this host's Bedrock provider cannot load AWS credentials from the recording shell, so the turn ran against a local 3B model instead, and that model answered the shell request in prose -- it wrote a Preamble and a fabricated Command Output block containing the expected text -- rather than emitting a tool call for the harness to translate. The tool_call, tool_call_update and session/request_permission shapes therefore stay in the synthesized session.jsonl beside this file. The model catalog is pruned the same way and for the same reason: models.availableModels and the `model` configOption list what the recording account is entitled to, including internal-only and unreleased entries, so only the product's own routing entry is kept. The served-model name in the usage block is emptied, and this capture carries no model catalog at all. One model name remains, in the turn's own text: codex warned that it had no metadata for the local model driving it. That is message body, not an enumeration -- editing it would damage the only thing this file is evidence of -- and the model is one built here from a public 3B checkpoint, so it discloses nothing about the recording host or account.
